PullRequest.Title: sessions: Scope Automations spinner to personal runs

Ref: #344711

## Motivation

Repository-owned automation runs currently make the primary-sidebar Automations entry look busy, even though that spinner is intended to reflect personal work. This PR limits the in-progress status to known personal automation definitions while leaving the existing session and completion status paths unchanged.

## Changes made

- Scope the Automations in-progress spinner to known personal automation definitions. Unknown and repository-owned run IDs no longer drive it.
- Add regression coverage for personal, repository-owned, mixed, and unknown running automations.

## Validation

- `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm.cmd run transpile-client` passed.
- `fnm exec --using=24.22.1 npm.cmd run test-browser-no-install -- --run src\vs\sessions\contrib\sessions\test\browser\sessionsList.test.ts --browser chromium` passed with 428 tests.

Scenarios.Scenario: Visible Automations custom view performs its periodic catalogue and history refresh while the Sessions list automation status remains observed.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The 60-second scheduler awaits cloud catalogue network refresh, publishes definitions, then awaits history network refresh and publishes runs. Each publication synchronously invalidates observed UI derivations before refresh progress continues.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh repository automation configuration, list definitions, and fetch definition details.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Per remembered/recent repository, one configuration call, paginated definition listing, then one detail call per definition in batches of five.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue calls occurred, but their publication did not invalidate automationStatus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalogue network completion precedes publication and the changed synchronous status scan.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List up to 50 runs per definition and fetch active task details.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One run-list call per definition with aggregate concurrency limited to four, plus detail reads for active runs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This was the sole periodic refresh publication that invalidated automationStatus.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: History completion publishes runs and causes the pre-existing automationStatus scan.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective cardinality is A definitions, up to 50 retained cloud runs per definition, and S automation sessions. The changed status derivation performs O(A + R*S) work on the catalogue publication; the existing runs publication performs O(R*S) again.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Definition requests are fetched in batches of five; history requests use a shared limiter of four; provider refreshes are sequenced. The status recomputations themselves are synchronous on the UI thread and are not coalesced across the separate catalogue and history publications.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cloud entries and history are cached, but successful polls replace each with fresh arrays even when content is unchanged. Provider and status derived values cache between invalidations; the new catalogue dependency defeats that cache for unchanged personal-ID membership.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added dependency, periodic timer, unconditional separate publications, and synchronous collection scan are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact catalogue, retained-history, and session sizes vary, so stall duration is uncertain; the API and code allow the multiplicative scan to become large.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable repeated-work amplification: the new dependency adds a second full run/session scan per periodic refresh when ID ownership membership is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Primary sidebar automation icon reacts to a run status or session status change.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The observable change synchronously recomputes automationStatus before the icon autorun updates DOM state; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is started by the changed code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: A automation definitions, R retained runs, and S automation sessions. The PR adds O(A) filtering/mapping/Set allocation to the existing O(R*S) scan.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single UI-thread reactive transaction; the main tree and optional navigation renderer own separate cached derivations when both are observed.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each renderer caches automationStatus until one dependency changes. The personal-ID Set is rebuilt on every run/session invalidation; no negative cache or cross-renderer sharing exists.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the allocation and synchronous path; low magnitude for this trigger independently of periodic refresh.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Definition counts are generally much smaller than retained-run/session combinations, so the incremental Set construction alone is unlikely to be user-visible.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding: the added O(A) work is bounded and normally dominated by the pre-existing run/session scan.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full two-file diff. One concrete repeated-work regression was identified on periodic catalogue refresh; report_finding was invoked but the reporting tool returned an execution failure on repeated valid submissions. No regression-fix learning signal was established.
